mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate compresses equity discount rates, generating positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as investors anticipate lower borrowing costs and increased liquidity.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS declines by at least 0.1% over the prior month.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly unemployment rate exceeding 4.0% signals deteriorating labor market conditions that trigger equity sell-offs, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 45% of months when UNRATE exceeds 4.0%.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in residential sales (RSAFS) and housing starts (HOUST) signal a weakening housing market that reduces consumer confidence and spending, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when both RSAFS and HOUST decline by at least 1% from the prior month.

mechanism_narrative: Declining industrial production (INDPRO below 105.0) indicates manufacturing sector weakness that reduces corporate earnings growth expectations, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when INDPRO is below 105.0.

mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate exceeding 2.5% with rising momentum signals aggressive monetary tightening that increases equity discount rates, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 45% of periods when FEDFUNDS exceeds 2.5% and rises by at least 0.1% in the prior month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in consumer spending (RSAFS) consistently boosts corporate revenue expectations, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as the economic expansion gains momentum.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when RSAFS increases by at least 0.5% from the prior month.

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent declines in employment growth (PAYEMS) and rising unemployment (UNRATE) signal a labor market slowdown that reduces consumer spending power, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when PAYEMS declines and UNRATE rises by at least 0.1% from the prior month.

mechanism_narrative: A rising industrial production index (INDPRO) indicates robust manufacturing activity that supports corporate earnings growth, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when INDPRO increases by at least 0.5% from the prior month.
